sections.heading: A considered choice of aircraft.

sections.heading: Explore the journey before requesting a quote
paragraphs: Start with the route and airport, then compare aircraft cabins and the complete cost of the journey. The flight request page is where you submit your itinerary; this service guide explains what to expect from sourcing and confirmation.

sections.heading: One complete travel brief.

sections.heading: Keep changes easy to follow.

Identify whether the party must return together and whether a substitute aircraft category is acceptable.

title: Private jet charter cost and pricing
description: Understand charter costs with hourly reference inputs, route examples, fees and a complete trip calculation. Request a written itinerary-specific quote from EXJET.

sections.heading: How much does aircraft charter cost?
paragraphs: A charter proposal prices a particular itinerary and aircraft. The total can include occupied flying, aircraft positioning, minimum flight time, crew arrangements, airport services and taxes. An attractive hourly number can therefore produce a higher trip total than a more expensive aircraft already near your departure airport.

EXJET supplies a written trip-specific proposal. The figures here are educational reference inputs and arithmetic examples, not EXJET tariffs, guaranteed fares or statements of current aircraft availability.

sections.heading: Hourly reference inputs by aircraft category
paragraphs: These approximate USD hourly figures are published by Global Charter and were checked on October 17, 2026. They provide an openly stated basis for the examples on this site. They are another provider’s category references, not quotations for EXJET flights. Individual aircraft and total trip charges may differ materially.

table.caption: Reference inputs for illustrations — USD per flight hour

sections.heading: A complete illustrative trip calculation
paragraphs: Consider an eight-passenger domestic flight with three occupied hours, one positioning hour and $2,000 of additional charges. This example assumes all $48,000 of pre-tax charges form taxable transportation and that the passenger journey has one taxable domestic segment. It is a budgeting exercise, not a quote.

table.caption: Hypothetical domestic trip with eight passengers

links.label: Ask EXJET for an actual trip proposal

sections.heading: Taxes and charges to confirm
paragraphs: For taxable U.S. passenger air transportation, IRS guidance sets a 7.5% percentage tax and a 2026 domestic segment tax of $5.30 per passenger per taxable segment. The applicable treatment depends on the itinerary and charge; the example should not be applied mechanically to international or exempt transportation.

Ask the provider to show the actual tax treatment and any separately payable charges in the written proposal. A fuel stop, an international sector or a different commercial arrangement can change the calculation.

sections.heading: Why one-way and round-trip pricing differ
paragraphs: A one-way passenger itinerary does not necessarily mean the aircraft only flies one sector. It may need to reach your departure airport and move again after landing. For a round trip, the operator may keep the aircraft nearby, reposition it, or provide a different aircraft for the return.

Compare the same dates, airports, passenger load and flexibility. Ask whether crew hotels, aircraft parking, waiting or daily minimums are included. For a meeting of uncertain length, agree the terms of a schedule change before accepting the offer.

sections.heading: Charges that need an explicit answer
paragraphs: A quote should identify what is included, what is conditional and what can be billed after the flight. Request the process for approving any additional expense.
bullets: Positioning, minimum usage and fuel treatment.
Airport handling, landing, parking and international services.
Crew overnight costs, waiting and itinerary changes.
Deicing, special catering, connectivity and ground transport.
Payment deadlines, quote validity, cancellation and substitution terms.

sections.heading: Choose the aircraft around the trip
paragraphs: Start with the passengers, baggage and airport requirements. Cabin width, seating layout, baggage access and connectivity can matter more than an advertised maximum range. A larger category may be useful for a long trip or a large group, but it is not automatically the best value for a short sector.

sections.heading: Route examples and empty legs
paragraphs: Use a route guide to understand early flight-time and cost illustrations, then request a proposal for your dates. Empty legs depend on another flight’s positioning needs; they can change or disappear. Ask for the exact commercial terms and a backup option before using one for an essential journey.

faqs.question: Is the hourly figure the total charter price?
faqs.answer: No. The total may include positioning, minimum flight charges, crew and airport costs, taxes and requested services. Compare the complete written price for the same itinerary.

faqs.question: Can EXJET quote a specific aircraft model?
faqs.answer: Yes. Include the preferred model and any acceptable alternatives. The quoted aircraft, operator, availability and final commercial terms must be confirmed for the travel dates.

faqs.question: How can I reduce the cost without changing the trip’s purpose?
faqs.answer: Offer realistic flexibility in departure time, nearby airports or aircraft type. Ask the advisor to compare complete proposals, including the effect on ground travel, rather than selecting the lowest hourly headline.

faqs.question: Are the route estimates live prices?
faqs.answer: No. They are transparent calculations using the reference inputs and time allowances described on this site. Only a current written proposal establishes the offer for a specific itinerary.

title: Aircraft management consulting
seoTitle: Aircraft Management Consulting & Owner Support | EXJET
description: Plan aircraft management with EXJET in Dallas. Compare operating budgets, provider proposals, maintenance coordination and reporting for your business jet.

sections.heading: An operating plan built around the owner.
paragraphs: EXJET provides aircraft management consulting for private owners, family offices and corporate aviation teams. Start with how the aircraft needs to work: annual utilization, typical missions, passenger requirements, home base and the level of owner involvement.

A useful management brief connects daily operations with the longer ownership plan. EXJET helps organize the requirements, compare provider proposals and clarify the decisions that need owner approval. The written engagement sets the services, reporting and responsibilities for your aircraft.

sections.heading: Compare the complete management proposal.
paragraphs: Review more than a monthly management fee. Understand what is included, what is passed through, who approves additional work and how the owner receives supporting records. Separate the operating budget from acquisition, financing and tax decisions.
bullets: Crew sourcing, training schedules and coverage requirements.
Home-base hangar, insurance and trip-support arrangements.
Scheduled maintenance, engine programs and downtime planning.
Operating budgets, expense approvals and owner reporting.
Charter-use objectives, availability priorities and operating responsibility.

sections.heading: Connect management with the next aircraft decision.
paragraphs: For an acquisition, define the operating structure before delivery. For an existing aircraft, begin with the current agreements, maintenance forecast and recurring service issues. For a sale, coordinate the transition of records, outstanding work and future travel coverage.

Family offices may need approval paths for several households. Corporate teams may need consolidated reporting and coordination with an existing flight department. EXJET’s consulting scope can be organized around those requirements without replacing the owner’s aviation, legal or tax advisers.

sections.heading: Dallas-based consulting, aircraft-specific scope.
paragraphs: Share the aircraft model, registration, base airport, utilization and current management arrangement. For Dallas–Fort Worth owners, identify the practical needs around Dallas Love Field, Addison or the aircraft’s actual home base. We can also discuss an aircraft based elsewhere.

The appointed operator retains operational control. Maintenance is performed and released by appropriately authorized providers. EXJET’s role, deliverables and provider relationships are set out in the agreed project scope.

faqs.question: What does aircraft management consulting cover?
faqs.answer: The consulting brief can cover owner objectives, operating budgets, management-provider selection, maintenance coordination, expense approvals and reporting. The agreed scope determines which tasks EXJET supports.

faqs.question: Can EXJET work with an existing flight department?
faqs.answer: Yes. Start by identifying the decisions or projects that need support, the current team’s responsibilities and the approval process. Consulting can focus on a specific workstream.

faqs.question: What should I send for an initial discussion?
faqs.answer: Send the aircraft type, registration, base, expected annual use, current arrangements and your main objectives. Avoid sending sensitive ownership or passenger documents until an appropriate exchange method is agreed.

title: Aircraft interior completions and refurbishment consulting
seoTitle: Aircraft Interior Completions & Refurbishment Consulting | EXJET
description: Plan a private jet interior refurbishment or completion with EXJET. Define cabin requirements, compare proposals and coordinate design, budget and downtime.

sections.heading: A cabin brief before a material selection.
paragraphs: EXJET supports aircraft interior completions and refurbishment through consulting, provider sourcing and project coordination. Begin with the way the cabin is used: working, dining, resting, travelling with family or accommodating a changing passenger group.

A new-aircraft completion and a refurbishment of an existing cabin are different projects. Identify the aircraft model, current layout, records, delivery objective and available downtime before comparing design proposals. The selected completion provider establishes technical feasibility and approval requirements.

sections.heading: Define the work in one coordinated scope.
paragraphs: A clear brief helps the owner compare proposals that cover the same work. Separate required repairs from aesthetic preferences, equipment changes and optional upgrades. Record the samples, drawings, assumptions and exclusions that belong to the accepted scope.
bullets: Seating, upholstery, carpets, veneers and surface finishes.
Cabin layout, galley, lavatory, storage and passenger needs.
Lighting, cabin controls, entertainment and connectivity.
Material documentation, engineering and applicable approvals.
Budget allowances, change orders, milestones and acceptance criteria.

sections.heading: Plan downtime and delivery together.
paragraphs: Discuss facility capacity, material lead times, inspection findings and the handover process before choosing a target completion date. Where appropriate, compare combining interior work with a scheduled maintenance event or connectivity installation.

EXJET helps keep the commercial brief, owner decisions and provider updates connected. The appointed facility is responsible for the technical work and required release documentation. Any schedule or price is confirmed in the provider’s written proposal.

sections.heading: Interior consulting for owners and acquisition teams.
paragraphs: For an aircraft purchase, assess the existing cabin against your mission before assuming a full refurbishment is necessary. For a family office or corporate owner, agree who signs off on design, expenditure and delivery. Dallas-based EXJET can help organize those decisions around your aircraft and chosen facility.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a completion and a refurbishment?
faqs.answer: A completion generally develops an aircraft cabin as part of its initial outfitting. A refurbishment updates an existing interior. The aircraft’s configuration and records determine the actual work and approval requirements.

faqs.question: Can interior work be combined with maintenance?
faqs.answer: It may be practical to coordinate the projects, but facility capabilities, materials, engineering and schedule must be reviewed together before confirming a combined downtime window.

faqs.question: Does EXJET perform the installation work?
faqs.answer: EXJET provides consulting and coordination. The selected completion or maintenance provider performs the technical work under the applicable authority.

title: EXJET editorial standards and sources
description: Learn how EXJET presents aircraft, airport and charter information. Review source standards, estimate limitations and the distinction between guides and live quotes.

sections.heading: Original guidance
paragraphs: The Flight Guide explains private aviation in practical language. Articles are written for EXJET and use original structure and explanations. Industry publications can inform research; their articles are not republished through close paraphrasing.

sections.heading: Sources and verification
paragraphs: We prioritize official aviation authorities, airport operators, and aircraft manufacturers for facts within their responsibility. Source links appear alongside the guides. Published aircraft data describes a reference configuration and does not establish the performance or equipment of a specific charter aircraft.

sections.heading: Dates and changes
paragraphs: Airport conditions, regulations, aircraft availability, and services can change. A guide's update date identifies its editorial version, not a guarantee that every operational detail remains current. The operating carrier confirms the details relevant to an actual flight.

sections.heading: Photography
paragraphs: Aircraft photographs identify the model shown and are representative unless the page expressly states otherwise. Manufacturer promotional photographs and owner-selected brand references do not imply that EXJET owns or operates the aircraft.

sections.heading: Corrections
paragraphs: If you notice an inaccurate statement or an outdated source, email sales@exjet.com with the page address and the point that needs attention.

sections.heading: How cost and time illustrations are prepared
paragraphs: Hourly inputs are attributed to the public source and observation date shown on the pricing page. Route examples multiply a stated planning time allowance by those inputs; they do not represent live inventory or a supplier offer. The operating carrier determines the actual flight plan and aircraft suitability.

Airport information is sourced primarily from airport authorities and regulators. We avoid treating old charts or a published runway length as confirmation that a specific aircraft can operate. Use current official aeronautical information through the operating crew.

title: Website accessibility

sections.heading: Navigation and reading

sections.heading: Tell us about a barrier
paragraphs: Email sales@exjet.com or call +1 407 747 5288. Include the page address, the task you were trying to complete, and your device or browser if you wish. Avoid sharing passwords or sensitive travel documents in the report.

title: Aircraft MRO consulting and maintenance coordination
seoTitle: Aircraft MRO Consulting & Maintenance Coordination | EXJET
description: Coordinate aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul with EXJET. Compare MRO proposals, plan downtime and define provider responsibilities for your business jet.

sections.heading: Maintenance decisions with a clear owner brief.
paragraphs: MRO means maintenance, repair and overhaul. EXJET provides aircraft MRO consulting and coordination for owners, family offices and corporate aviation teams. The starting point is the aircraft’s records, upcoming maintenance events and the owner’s operating priorities.

Bring the model, serial number, registration, aircraft location and a summary of the required work. Your maintenance team or selected provider determines the technical requirements. EXJET helps organize the commercial scope, compare suitable proposals and coordinate the owner’s decisions.

sections.heading: Compare scope, capability and total downtime.
paragraphs: A useful comparison includes more than the quoted labor rate. Identify the work package, exclusions, parts assumptions, program coverage, facility capability and proposed schedule. Agree how additional findings will be reported and authorized.
bullets: Scheduled inspections and maintenance-event planning.
Engine, APU and component workstream coordination.
Pre-purchase inspection and findings follow-up.
Avionics, connectivity and cabin-upgrade planning.
Aircraft positioning, parts logistics and downtime contingencies.
Change approval, invoice review and handover records.

sections.heading: Coordinate the work around your operating calendar.
paragraphs: For a planned visit, work backward from the aircraft’s next essential mission and review the provider’s available capacity. Discuss whether interior or connectivity projects can be combined without creating an impractical delivery deadline.

For an urgent maintenance issue, provide the aircraft location and a concise description from the crew or maintenance team. Technical troubleshooting, dispatch decisions and return-to-service approval remain with appropriately authorized personnel; consulting does not replace those decisions.

sections.heading: Dallas-based support for aircraft owners.
paragraphs: EXJET’s Dallas base supports discussions with owners in the Dallas–Fort Worth area and aircraft teams coordinating work elsewhere. Facility selection should follow the aircraft, required approvals, work scope and schedule. A city name alone does not establish that a provider can perform the work.

EXJET provides consulting and coordination; the appointed maintenance provider performs the work and supplies the required technical records. Provider selection, availability, price and schedule are confirmed for each project.

faqs.question: What does MRO stand for in aviation?
faqs.answer: MRO stands for maintenance, repair and overhaul. It covers a range of aircraft technical work; the precise scope depends on the aircraft, its records and the required maintenance event.

faqs.question: Can EXJET help compare maintenance proposals?
faqs.answer: Yes. EXJET can help organize the project brief and compare the commercial scope, exclusions, schedule and owner-approval requirements. The technical provider confirms capability and applicable authorization.

faqs.question: Is EXJET the repair station?
faqs.answer: EXJET provides MRO consulting and coordination. The appointed, appropriately authorized maintenance provider performs and releases the technical work.

title: Starlink aviation installation consulting
seoTitle: Starlink Aircraft Installation Consulting & Coordination | EXJET
description: Plan Starlink installation for your business jet with EXJET. Review aircraft eligibility, installer proposals, downtime, cabin requirements and service activation.

sections.heading: Start with the aircraft, then the connection.
paragraphs: EXJET provides Starlink aviation installation consulting and coordination for business jet owners, family offices and corporate aviation teams. The project begins with the aircraft model, serial number, registration, current connectivity equipment and intended use.

Eligibility is aircraft-specific. Confirm the applicable approved installation route, configuration and supporting documentation with the selected installer before ordering hardware or booking downtime. A model name in a general guide is not confirmation that a particular aircraft is ready for installation.

sections.heading: Build a complete installation brief.
paragraphs: Define what passengers need to do in the cabin, how the crew will support the system and who will manage the service account. Corporate or family-office requirements may include device access, network administration and a clear support contact.
bullets: Aircraft model, serial number and registration jurisdiction.
Existing antenna, avionics and cabin network configuration.
Applicable approvals and installer capability.
Hardware, installation, subscription and support scope.
Downtime window and other planned maintenance or interior work.
Ground testing, documentation, activation and owner handover.

sections.heading: Compare installation and ongoing service separately.
paragraphs: Ask for a proposal that separates equipment, engineering, labor, testing, any required cabin-network work and ongoing service. Confirm exclusions and what happens if inspection reveals additional work. EXJET helps coordinate the questions and compare the written proposals.

For an acquisition or refurbishment, review connectivity early enough to include it in the ownership and downtime plan. The selected installer confirms the technical work, approval pathway and delivery schedule. Performance, coverage and service terms should be checked directly against current Starlink documentation.

sections.heading: One contact for the owner’s project.
paragraphs: Dallas-based EXJET can help organize an installation brief for your aircraft and chosen facility. Send the aircraft details, location, preferred timing and current connectivity setup to start the discussion.

EXJET provides consulting and coordination. Installation is performed by the selected appropriately authorized provider. Starlink availability, aircraft eligibility and service terms require confirmation for the specific project; EXJET does not present itself as Starlink or as an authorized installer.

faqs.question: Can Starlink be installed on any private jet?
faqs.answer: Do not assume universal eligibility. The selected installer must confirm the current approval route and configuration for the aircraft model, serial number and registration jurisdiction.

faqs.question: How much does aircraft Starlink installation cost?
faqs.answer: Request an aircraft-specific written proposal covering hardware, installation, engineering, testing, cabin-network work and ongoing service. EXJET does not publish a fixed price for an unassessed aircraft.

faqs.question: Can installation be coordinated with other aircraft work?
faqs.answer: It may be possible to combine installation with maintenance or interior work. Confirm the facility’s capability, approvals, parts availability and schedule before committing to a combined project.

title: Business aviation consulting for owners and corporate teams
seoTitle: Business Aviation Consulting for Family Offices & Corporations | EXJET
description: EXJET aviation consulting connects charter, ownership and technical projects for family offices and corporate teams. Build a clear mission, budget and decision brief.

sections.heading: Choose the aviation solution around the mission.
paragraphs: EXJET is a business aviation solutions company based in Dallas. Our consulting approach connects the decisions around travel, aircraft ownership and technical projects so that an owner, executive assistant or corporate team can work from one clear brief.

Start with the outcomes that matter: the places people need to reach, how frequently they travel, the required cabin, schedule flexibility and approval process. For an aircraft project, add the ownership objectives, current condition and available downtime.

sections.heading: A decision brief for each stakeholder.
paragraphs: An executive assistant may need a reliable itinerary and a clear process for late changes. A family office may need to coordinate several principals, control distribution of sensitive information and compare ownership with charter. A corporate flight department may need supplemental capacity or support for an aircraft project.

EXJET helps organize those requirements before comparing options. Finance, procurement, legal and the operating team should agree on the decisions they own, the records they need and the approval milestones.
bullets: Mission profile and passenger requirements.
Charter, supplemental lift or ownership objectives.
Budget assumptions and complete proposal comparisons.
Operating-provider and technical-provider responsibilities.
Project milestones, approvals and communication preferences.

sections.heading: Connect the flight with the ownership lifecycle.
paragraphs: A purchase decision can affect management, maintenance, interior and connectivity requirements for years. A cabin project can affect aircraft availability. A maintenance event can create a temporary need for charter. Planning these decisions together helps keep the commercial brief consistent.

The seven EXJET service areas cover charter, group charter, sales and acquisitions, aircraft management, MRO, interior completions and Starlink installation coordination. Each engagement has a defined scope; operating and technical work remains with the appropriately authorized provider.

sections.heading: Dallas expertise, mission-led geographic planning.
paragraphs: For Dallas–Fort Worth travel, compare Dallas Love Field and Addison against the meeting address, aircraft requirements and ground transfer. For New York, South Florida or Los Angeles trips, use the actual destination and operating assessment to narrow the airport options. Avoid choosing an airport solely because it is the most familiar name.
Share the next decision, the expected timeline and who is involved. EXJET can help define a consulting brief that connects the right service to the actual business or ownership requirement.

faqs.question: Who is business aviation consulting for?
faqs.answer: EXJET works with aircraft owners, corporate aviation and travel teams, executive assistants and family offices that need help organizing charter, ownership or technical-project decisions.

faqs.question: Can a consulting engagement focus on one project?
faqs.answer: Yes. Define the objective, scope, timeline and required deliverables with EXJET. A brief may cover an aircraft acquisition, a management review, maintenance coordination or a cabin-connectivity project.

faqs.question: Does consulting replace the operating carrier or technical provider?
faqs.answer: No. The operating carrier controls the flight, and the selected authorized technical provider performs maintenance or installation work. EXJET coordinates the client brief and agreed consulting workstreams.
